profiles.identity_notes: Kenny has two stocks: 'Geosmin (0.1% in TEC) # diluted 2026-05-11 from original 1% stock' and 'Geosmin (1% in TEC)' (inventory.txt lines 84-85). The repo YAML lists PW 5YW13682 (1% in DPG) as the main SKU and 5YW18061 (1% in TEC) as an alternate; Kenny's TEC carrier matches 5YW18061, read live here. Both PW pages carry the same odour text. Producer: Pell Wall and Fraterworks both name IFF as manufacturer (Pell Wall: 'First isolated by Bush Boake Allen (now part of IFF)'; 'Manufacturer: IFF / Pell Wall'); IFF's own page was not found. Geosmin is a trace material: the neat odour is rarely smelled and every source quoted is of a 0.01-1% dilution or of ng/L water solutions. Natural (-)-geosmin has about an 11x lower threshold than (+) (Polak & Provasi 1992), so the stereo make-up of the trade material matters for strength but no source here states it. Engine text ('earthy 9, mineral 6, green 2', note 'heart') is unsourced; no source below uses 'mineral'.

profiles.identity_notes: Leafovert(R) is Symrise's trade name (TGSC lists it as Symrise '131380 Leafovert (R)') for a single molecule, cis-3-hexenyl methyl carbonate: the same molecule as IFF Liffarome(TM) (also sold as Vertelione, Vertocarb, Greenarome, Laniffarome, muguet carbonate, per TGSC synonyms). The PW page does NOT support 'PW base/specialty': PW 4GI15439 is badged 'Aroma Ingredients', gives one CAS (67633-96-9), says 'Not found in nature', and its Synonyms block lists the chemical names plus 'leafovert : liffarome : vertelione : vertocarb : PerfumersWorld Authentic Perfumery Material'. PW does not name the producer of its Leafovert. PW's one-line description repeats Bedoukian's text word for word and its Perfume-Uses repeats IFF's Liffarome text, and PW sells Liffarome separately (4GI24147) with the same Odour=> line, so the PW text is a compilation, not a Symrise text. Kenny's bottle is neat (inventory.txt line 82: 'Leafovert (neat)  # user-confirmed NEAT 2026-08-07'). Pyrfume Leffingwell row 'cis-hexenyl methyl carbonate' (CID 6437112) carries an (E) SMILES; its flags are taken as for the named material, with that caveat.

profiles.identity_notes: Kenny's stock is 'Osmanthus Absolute (10% in DPG)' (inventory.txt line 167), a 'premium' absolute he diluted himself by weight (overlay INV-USER-20261008-V22-001, Kenny: 'Osmanthus is made by w/w'). The supplier of the neat absolute is not recorded; the 2026-08-30 supplier census marks the PW match AMBIGUOUS_EXACT_NAME (8ND00346 neat / 5ND10990 10% in DPG). A separate neat 'Osmanthus Absolute (volume grade)' bottle exists (inventory.txt line 177, 'lower β-ionone content than premium'); it is a different stock and not covered here. LABELLED PROXY: the closest published identity is Osmanthus fragrans Lour. (Oleaceae) flower absolute from China, made by volatile-solvent extraction of brine-preserved flowers to a concrete, then ethanol purification to the absolute (Givaudan, Robertet, Biolandes agree; Arctander 1960: petroleum-ether concrete, then alcohol extraction). Givaudan says the leathery/animal facet comes from the brining step. Grades differ: Givaudan's 'Osmanthus Gold Absolute' is described as 'fresher and lighter than the classic Osmanthus Absolute', and IFF sells a less-coloured 'MD 50 PCT' grade; which grade 'premium' means is unknown. Descriptors are for the neat absolute; Kenny's bottle is 10% in DPG. The engine's own text ('floral 6, fruity 4, leather 3, sweet 2') is unsourced.

profiles.identity_notes: Engine profile key 'Peppermint Essential Oil'. Kenny's stocks: 'Peppermint Essential Oil (Mentha piperita, India) # added 2026-06-15 - steam-distilled; 100% pure; INCI: Mentha Piperita Oil; crisp herbal-fresh menthol cooling' (inventory.txt line 86, neat) and 'Peppermint EO (10% v/v in ethanol)' (line 87, a working dilution Kenny made 2026-09-08). The supplier is not named. The census matched PW 7BB00360 by name only ('EXACT_NAME_SKU'), but PW's page names no species or origin, while Kenny's label says India, so the PW match is unconfirmed. LABELLED PROXY: Mentha piperita (Mentha x piperita, Lamiaceae) essential oil, steam-distilled from the flowering tops / aerial parts, India origin: Givaudan 'Peppermint Oil India' and TGSC 'peppermint oil india' are the closest published identities. Robertet's India product is a column 'fraction', not a whole oil, so it is a weaker proxy. Arctander warns that outside the USA 'peppermint oil' is often adulterated with Mentha arvensis (cornmint) oil; nothing here can test Kenny's bottle for that. The Dravnieks atlas has Spearmint Oil and l-Menthol but no peppermint oil; they are listed as labelled analogues only. The engine's text ('herbal 8, fresh 5, sweet 3, green 2') is unsourced and has no 'minty' or 'cooling' word.

profiles.identity_notes: LABELLED PROXY IDENTITY. Kenny's bottle is 'Spike Lavender EO (neat / as supplied)' (inventory.txt line 349, added 2026-04-29; census perfumersworld_match_state NO_EXACT_PW_MATCH), so its supplier, origin and batch are unrecorded. Per Kenny's rule the closest published identity is used: Lavandula latifolia Medik. (syn. L. spica), Lamiaceae; part = flowering tops; process = steam (water-steam) distillation; main origin Spain (also S. France). Robertet BIO TDS: 'Used part : Flowering top ... Manufacturing method : By water-steam distillation of flowering tops ... Country of origin : Spain'. TGSC: 'essential oil distilled from the flowering herbs of the lavender, lavandula latifolia (syn: lavandula spica), labiatae'. Typical composition (Robertet BIO TDS ranges): linalool 34-50%, 1,8-cineole 16-39%, camphor 8-16%, beta-pinene 1-4%, alpha-pinene 0.5-4%, trans-alpha-bisabolene 0.4-2.5%. Not the same as true lavender (L. angustifolia, linalyl-acetate rich) nor lavandin (hybrid). Kenny's own inventory note: 'camphoraceous lavender, more aromatic/masculine and less soft-floral than Lavender EO' (kenny_known left empty as instructed). Excellentia warns: 'Spike Lavender is easily adulterated with eucalyptus fractions, synthetic Linalool and synthetic or natural Camphor.'
